Why do stars twinkle while planets do not twinkle?
options: Stars are point-sized distant sources; starlight refracts continuously through fluctuating atmospheric air density, caus
explanation: Stars are point-sized distant sources; starlight refracts continuously through fluctuating atmospheric air density, causing apparent position and brightness to flicker. Planets are close extended sources, so point light variations average out to zero.

question: Why is sunrise seen 2 minutes before actual horizon crossing?
options: Light rays from below horizon refract through progressively denser air layers, bending downward so the sun appears appar
explanation: Light rays from below horizon refract through progressively denser air layers, bending downward so the sun appears apparent above horizon.

explanation: A rainbow is a natural spectrum caused by dispersion of sunlight by spherical raindrops. 1. Refraction & Dispersion: Sunlight entering raindrop refracts and splits into colors. 2.
